title: EE Reveals UK iPhone Handoff Pricing: New Costs, Plans & Details Unveiled by 9to5Mac
body:
EE has become the first UK mobile operator to roll out a dedicated pricing plan for Apple’s iPhone Handoff feature, unveiling the details alongside its launch of the iPhone Duo preorder programme. The new “iPhone Handoff” add‑on will cost £3 per month, or £30 annually, and is available to existing EE customers who upgrade to a compatible iPhone model. The move signals a growing willingness among carriers to monetise Apple’s continuity services, while also giving UK users a clearer cost structure for a feature that previously relied on bundled data plans or hidden fees.

The iPhone Handoff service allows users to start an activity—such as drafting an email, browsing a website, or listening to music—on one Apple device and seamlessly continue it on another, provided both are signed into the same iCloud account and are on the same Wi‑Fi or cellular network. Although the functionality has been part of iOS and macOS for several years, its reliance on a stable internet connection means that mobile operators have historically bundled the capability into broader data packages, making it difficult for consumers to understand the exact price they are paying for the service. EE’s decision to separate Handoff into a distinct, low‑cost subscription could set a precedent for other carriers in the region.

Industry analysts view EE’s pricing strategy as a calculated response to both consumer demand and competitive pressure. The UK market has seen a surge in premium smartphone adoption, with Apple’s iPhone 15 series driving record sales in the last quarter. As more users integrate multiple Apple devices into their daily routines, the value proposition of continuity features like Handoff becomes more tangible. By offering a modest monthly fee, EE can capture revenue from a segment of customers who might otherwise forgo the service due to ambiguous pricing, while also differentiating its portfolio from rivals such as Vodafone and Three, which have yet to announce similar standalone options.

From a technical standpoint, the Handoff add‑on leverages EE’s 5G network to minimise latency and ensure a fluid handover experience. The carrier has confirmed that the service will work across all 5G‑enabled iPhone models released from the iPhone 8 onward, as long as the device runs iOS 17 or later. Existing EE customers can activate the feature through the My EE app or via the company’s website, where they will be prompted to verify their Apple ID and enable the “Continuity” settings on each device. The subscription can be added to any post‑pay or pay‑as‑you‑go plan, and there are no additional data charges beyond the standard allowance.

Consumer reaction has been cautiously optimistic. Early adopters appreciate the transparency of a flat‑fee model, noting that it removes the guesswork associated with data‑heavy continuity usage. However, some critics argue that the fee, albeit modest, could be seen as double‑charging users who already pay for generous data caps. EE has responded by highlighting that the Handoff service does not consume additional data beyond what is already allocated to the user’s plan, and that the subscription simply unlocks a premium feature that would otherwise be inaccessible on lower‑tier contracts.

Looking ahead, EE’s rollout may prompt a broader industry shift toward itemised pricing for ecosystem‑specific services. As Apple continues to expand its suite of continuity tools—such as Universal Control, AirPlay to Mac, and the upcoming “iPhone as a Mac” capability—carriers could find new revenue streams by packaging these functionalities separately. For UK consumers, the introduction of a clear, affordable Handoff subscription could accelerate the adoption of Apple’s cross‑device workflow, reinforcing the ecosystem’s appeal and potentially influencing future handset purchasing decisions.
